title: Inktrap
direction: Assertive precision: heavy custom lowercase lettering with deep, deliberate ink traps carved at one angle into every join
rationale: Ink traps are the type designer's own craft detail; exaggerated and made consistent, they show that Markilo is made by people who draw letters, not by a generator
semantics: craft; precision; studio-grade; type specimen; confident

pitch.idea: A heavy lowercase word cut like a type designer's proof: every join of m, a, r and k carries the same deep ink trap, and the k-i-l stems rise above the font's ascenders into one tall, even skyline.
strengths: the ink trap is a detail only people who draw type would make, so it says studio, not generator
one cut geometry (same depth, same funnel) repeated at eight joins reads as a system
the raised k-i-l stems give the word a silhouette no stock grotesque has (typeset likeness 0.74)
the trapped k, where three traps converge, stands alone as the icon
weaknesses: the icon is still a letter k, the weakest kind of icon, and its traps fill in below 32 px where it is just a heavy k
the traps disappear below about 24 px wordmark height, so small uses rely on the tall stems alone
the slits in the a and the lower k join can read as chips at mid sizes (48-96 px)
stem proportions are Schibsted's, so the face is recognisable to type people
